descripcion_es: Growth, employment, inflation, markets and trade: the basic vocabulary of the financial press.
resumen: Common economic vocabulary in the press and in reports: macroeconomics, the labour market, prices, business and foreign trade. Essential for summarising news and presenting economic topics in English.

explicacion.texto: Economic English has many words similar to Spanish, but also differences in usage: “economics” is the science and “economy” is the economy of a country; “benefit” is not an accounting “beneficio” (that is “profit”).

filas: total value of goods and services produced in a country (es: PIB)
increase in output / to increase (es: crecimiento / crecer)
Growth slowed in the second quarter.
period of falling output / slowdown (es: recesión / desaceleración)
return to growth after a crisis (es: recuperación)
general rise / fall in prices (es: inflación / deflación)
percentage charged for borrowing money (es: tipo de interés)
The central bank raised interest rates.
money owed by the state / annual shortfall (es: deuda pública / déficit)
The deficit narrowed to 3% of GDP.
money the state collects in taxes (es: recaudación fiscal)
money spent by the state (es: gasto público)
percentage of the labour force without a job (es: tasa de paro)
people working or looking for work (in a country) (es: población activa)
Women make up half the labour force.
The company has a workforce of 500.
pay (per hour or week) / pay (per year) (es: salarios / sueldo)
Wages have not kept up with prices.
to employ / to dismiss (for economic reasons) (es: contratar / despedir)
money gained / money lost (es: beneficio / pérdida)
The bank made a record profit.
income from sales / total sales (es: ingresos / facturación)
owner of shares in a company (es: accionista)
joining of two companies / purchase of one company by another (often hostile) (es: fusión / adquisición)
what is offered and what is wanted (es: oferta y demanda)
Prices depend on supply and demand.
percentage of a market's sales (es: cuota de mercado)
They lost market share to rivals.
goods sold abroad / goods bought from abroad (es: exportaciones / importaciones)
Exports account for a third of GDP.
exports above / below imports (es: superávit / déficit comercial)
Germany runs a large trade surplus.
The US imposed tariffs on steel.
network from raw materials to the customer (es: cadena de suministro)
putting money into something / person who does so (es: inversión / inversor)
a country's economic system / the science (es: la economía de un país / la economía como ciencia)

items: Typical verbs: boost (to push up), curb (to restrain), stimulate, tighten / ease (to make monetary policy stricter / looser).
“Economic” = relating to the economy; “economical” = cheap, saving money (Spanish uses “económico” for both).

ejemplos.frase: The economy grew faster than expected in the first quarter.
ejemplos.traduccion: La economía creció más de lo previsto en el primer trimestre.

ejemplos.frase: Rising energy prices pushed inflation above 5%.
ejemplos.traduccion: La subida de los precios de la energía llevó la inflación por encima del 5%.

ejemplos.frase: The company reported a loss for the third year in a row.
ejemplos.traduccion: La empresa registró pérdidas por tercer año consecutivo.

ejemplos.frase: Small businesses struggle to get credit during a downturn.
ejemplos.traduccion: A las pequeñas empresas les cuesta conseguir crédito en una desaceleración.

ejemplos.frase: The new tariffs could disrupt supply chains across Europe.
ejemplos.traduccion: Los nuevos aranceles podrían alterar las cadenas de suministro en toda Europa.

ejemplos.frase: My car is very economical: it uses very little fuel.
ejemplos.traduccion: Mi coche es muy económico: gasta muy poco combustible.

errores_hispanohablantes.nota: The academic discipline is “economics”; “economy” is the economy of a country.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: The company had big benefits this year.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: The company made big profits this year.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Accounting profit is “profit”; “benefit” is an advantage or a welfare payment.
Abstract nouns used in a general sense take no article.

ejercicios.frase: The central bank decided to raise interest ___ by half a point.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes interest rate (es: tipo de interés). The clue is raise… by half a point, typical of monetary policy. Rate is the word that expresses a proportion or ratio per unit; it is plural because we are talking about rates in general.
ejercicios.traduccion: El banco central decidió subir los tipos de interés medio punto.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Calque of “tipo de interés”: in English it is interest rate.
The sentence talks about rates in general and the plural is the usual form: interest rates.
Ratio is a relationship between two quantities; the interest rate is rate.

glosario.definicion_l: the percentage of a sum of money charged for its use
a government monetary authority that issues currency and regulates the supply of credit and holds the reserves of other banks and sells new issues of…

ejercicios.frase: He has a degree in ___ from the LSE.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card distinguishes economics (the science) from economy (the economy of a country). The clue is a degree in, which requires an academic discipline. Economics, despite the -s, is singular and uncountable, like mathematics.
ejercicios.traduccion: Es licenciado en Economía por la LSE.

por_opcion.economy: Incorrect: economy is the economy of a country or region, not the degree subject.
por_opcion.economics: Correct: economics is the science of economics, what you study at university.
por_opcion.economical: Incorrect: it is an adjective (cheap, saving money), not a noun.

glosario.definicion_l: the branch of social science that deals with the production and distribution and consumption of goods and services and their management
a position on a scale of intensity or amount or quality · a specific identifiable position in a continuum or series or especially in a process

ejercicios.frase: The firm made a net ___ of 3 million euros.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card warns that benefit is not accounting profit: that is profit. The clue is net and the figure in euros, which point to the income statement. The collocation is make a profit.
ejercicios.traduccion: La empresa obtuvo un beneficio neto de 3 millones de euros.

por_opcion.benefit: Incorrect: benefit is an advantage or a welfare payment (social benefits); it is not the accounting result.
por_opcion.profit: Correct: profit is a company's earnings; make a net profit.
por_opcion.winning: Incorrect: winning means victorious or the act of winning; money won in a game is winnings, never business profit.

glosario.definicion_l: the excess of revenues over outlays in a given period of time (including depreciation and other non-cash expenses) · the advantageous quality of being beneficial
remaining after all deductions · conclusive in a process or progression
marked by firm determination or resolution; not shakable · not soft or yielding to pressure

ejercicios.frase: The US imposed a 25% ___ on imported steel.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives tariff (es: arancel), the tax on imports. The clue is imposed… on imported steel. Duty is also accepted; it refers to a customs charge or tax, with a very similar meaning.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: A tax on imports is a “tariff” (also “duty”).
ejercicios.traduccion: Estados Unidos impuso un arancel del 25% al acero importado.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The English word is required: tariff.
Tax is a tax in general; the tax on imports has its own name: tariff or duty.
It is spelt with two f's: tariff.

glosario.definicion_l: a government tax on imports or exports · charge a tariff

an alloy of iron with small amounts of carbon; widely used in construction; mechanical properties can be varied over a wide range · a cutting or thrusting weapon that has a long metal blade and a hilt with a hand guard

ejercicios.frase: The factory closed and 300 workers were ___.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes to lay off = to dismiss for economic reasons (not for bad behaviour, which would be fire or dismiss). The clue is The factory closed: the dismissals are due to the closure. In the passive: were laid off.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “To lay off” means to dismiss for economic reasons.
ejercicios.traduccion: La fábrica cerró y despidieron a 300 trabajadores.

por_opcion.laid off: Correct: lay off = to dismiss for economic reasons.
por_opcion.laid out: Incorrect: lay out means to arrange, design or set out (lay out a plan).
por_opcion.hired: Incorrect: hire means to employ, the opposite of what happens when the factory closes.
por_opcion.put off: Incorrect: put off means to postpone or to discourage.

glosario.definicion_l: a plant consisting of one or more buildings with facilities for manufacturing

ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives GDP (gross domestic product) (es: PIB). English acronyms follow the English word order of the phrase, which is why they do not match the Spanish ones. The clue is grew by 2.5%, the typical growth figure.
ejercicios.traduccion: El PIB de España creció un 2,5% el año pasado.

errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the Spanish acronym; in English it is GDP.
GNP is gross national product, a different indicator; the one required is GDP.

ejercicios.frase: The interest type has gone up again.
respuestas: The interest rate has gone up again.
ejercicios.explicacion: This is one of the mistakes in the card: “tipo de interés” is interest rate, never interest type. Type means kind or sort, in the sense of a category. The rest of the sentence is correct.
ejercicios.traduccion: El tipo de interés ha vuelto a subir.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The interest type has gone up again.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: interest type is a calque.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The interest ratio has gone up again.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Ratio is a proportion between two quantities; the interest rate is rate.

glosario.definicion_l: the percentage of a sum of money charged for its use

ejercicios.frase: Small cars are more economic to run.
respuestas: Small cars are more economical to run.
Small cars are cheaper to run.
ejercicios.explicacion: The list in the card distinguishes economic (relating to the economy: economic growth) from economical (cheap, saving money). The clue is to run: we are talking about the cost of using the car, about saving money. Cheaper to run is also accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Saving money” is “economical”; “economic” refers to the economy.
ejercicios.traduccion: Los coches pequeños son más económicos de mantener.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Small cars are more economic to run.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: economic refers to the economy, not to saving.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Small cars are more economics to run.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Economics is a noun (the science); you need the adjective economical.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Small cars are more cheap to run.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Cheap has its own comparative: cheaper, not more cheap.

glosario.definicion_l: using the minimum of time or resources necessary for effectiveness · of or relating to an economy, the system of production and management of material wealth
of or relating to an economy, the system of production and management of material wealth · of or relating to the science of economics

ejercicios.frase: Exports exceeded imports, so the country ran a trade ___.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives trade surplus (es: superávit comercial) and trade deficit (es: déficit comercial). The clue is Exports exceeded imports: if a country sells abroad more than it buys, there is a surplus. The collocation is run a surplus.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: If exports exceed imports there is a “surplus”.
ejercicios.traduccion: Las exportaciones superaron a las importaciones, así que el país tuvo superávit comercial.

por_opcion.surplus: Correct: more exports than imports = trade surplus.
por_opcion.deficit: Incorrect: a trade deficit occurs when imports exceed exports.
por_opcion.debt: Incorrect: debt is a stock concept, not the trade balance.

glosario.definicion_l: an excess of exports over imports.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with one word (es: cuota de mercado).
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes market share (es: cuota de mercado). Share is the part or portion that belongs to someone. The clue is gaining market…, a fixed collocation; its opposite is lose market share.
ejercicios.traduccion: Los competidores más pequeños están ganando cuota de mercado.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Calque of “cuota”: quota is a fixed limit or allocation (import quota), not market share.
Market part does not exist; you say market share.

glosario.definicion_l: as a rival in a competition · the contestant you hope to defeat

ejercicios.frase: After two years of recession, the economy is finally in ___.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives recovery = (economic) recovery. The clue is After two years of recession and the preposition in, which requires a noun: in recovery. Recuperation exists, but it is used for physical recovery or rest.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Economic recovery is “recovery”; “recuperation” is physical recovery.
ejercicios.traduccion: Tras dos años de recesión, la economía por fin está en recuperación.

por_opcion.recuperation: Incorrect: it is used for a person's physical recovery; it is the calque of “recuperación”.
por_opcion.recovering: Incorrect: after in you need a noun; you would say the economy is recovering, without in.

glosario.definicion_l: return to an original state · gradual healing (through rest) after sickness or injury
the state of the economy declines; a widespread decline in the GDP and employment and trade lasting from six months to a year · a small concavity

ejercicios.frase: The board must explain the losses to its ___.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives shareholder (es: accionista); in American English also stockholder. The clue is the board (board of directors) accounting for the losses: the people addressed are the owners of the company. It is plural.
ejercicios.traduccion: El consejo de administración debe explicar las pérdidas a sus accionistas.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Its refers to the company and there are several shareholders: shareholders.
Calque of “accionistas”: it does not exist in English.
Stakeholders are all the interested parties (employees, customers, shareholders); the owners of shares are shareholders.

glosario.definicion_l: someone who holds shares of stock in a corporation
a committee having supervisory powers · a stout length of sawn timber; made in a wide variety of sizes and used for many purposes
something lost (especially money lost at gambling)

ejercicios.frase: The unemployment is falling in most regions.
respuestas: Unemployment is falling in most regions.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card includes this mistake: abstract nouns used in a general sense take no article in English. Unemployment, like inflation or growth, is used without the when talking about the phenomenon in general. Just remove The.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: In a general sense, “unemployment” takes no article.
ejercicios.traduccion: El paro está bajando en la mayoría de las regiones.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The unemployment is falling in most regions.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: the is not needed.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The unemployment is falling in the most regions.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Both articles are unnecessary: unemployment in a general sense and most regions take no the.

glosario.definicion_l: the state of being unemployed or not having a job
(superlative of ‘many’ used with count nouns and often preceded by ‘the’) quantifier meaning the greatest in number

respuestas: The pandemic disrupted global supply chains
ejercicios.explicacion: It is a subject + verb + object sentence. The table includes supply chain (es: cadena de suministro), a compound noun; global is an adjective and in English it goes before the whole compound: global supply chains. Disrupt means to interrupt or disturb.
ejercicios.traduccion: La pandemia alteró las cadenas de suministro mundiales.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The pandemic disrupted supply chains global
errores_previstos.explicacion: Calque of the Spanish “cadenas de suministro mundiales”: the adjective goes first.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The pandemic disrupted global chains supply
errores_previstos.explicacion: In the compound, supply modifies chains and goes first: supply chains.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with a verb (to push up).
ejercicios.frase: Lower taxes are meant to ___ consumer spending.
ejercicios.explicacion: The list of typical verbs in the card gives boost (to push up) and stimulate. The clue is Lower taxes are meant to…: the aim is to increase consumption. Spur and encourage are also accepted, with a very similar meaning.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Boost” or “stimulate” = to push up, to encourage.
ejercicios.traduccion: La bajada de impuestos pretende impulsar el gasto de los consumidores.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Curb means to restrain, the opposite of what lowering taxes aims to do.
Calque of “impulsar”: impulse is a noun, not used as a verb in this sense.
After are meant to comes the infinitive: boost.

descripcion_larga_es: Common economic vocabulary in the press and in reports: macroeconomics (GDP, inflation, interest rates), the labour market, business (profit, turnover, shareholders) and foreign trade (tariffs, trade surplus). It is essential for summarising news and presenting economic topics in English, and it has false friends that trip up even economists: economy versus economics, benefit versus profit, or “tipo de interés” versus interest rate.

contexto.que_es: It is the basic vocabulary of economics and business in English: macroeconomic indicators (GDP, inflation, deficit), the labour market (unemployment rate, workforce, lay off), company results (profit, loss, turnover) and foreign trade (exports, tariffs, supply chains).
contexto.por_que_importa: For a candidate with an economics profile, this is the vocabulary used to read international reports and discuss topics in English. False friends (economy for economics, benefit for profit, interest type) produce mistakes that are very visible to an examining board, because they affect basic concepts of the subject.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: When summarising economic news, commenting on growth or employment data, talking about monetary or trade policy and explaining company results. The signals are figures, percentages and trend verbs (grow, fall, raise, boost). Spanish speakers tend to calque “tipo de interés”, “beneficio” or “estudiar economía” and to put an article before abstract nouns such as unemployment.
